changelog: - **One person, two worlds: the URL you sign in on decides the product** (#2590, epic #2348). `User.email` is no longer globally unique — the database keeps `@@unique([email, orgId])` and the app keeps the real rule, at most one account per (e-mail, world), by calling `emailTakenInWorld()`/`emailTakenInOrgWorld()` before every user create (MySQL treats a NULL `orgId` as distinct, so the index alone cannot). A world is the vertical of the user's organization (derived, never stored on the user); the host picks it (`src/lib/hostWorld.ts`, `MARKETING_HOSTS`), and `src/lib/userWorld.ts` is the only place an e-mail address becomes a user row. Sign-in takes the account in the host's world; the right password for an account that lives only in the other world answers `WRONG_WORLD_<VERTICAL>`, which the sign-in page turns into a localized message and a link to the other product's `/auth/signin` (origins computed server-side by `worldOrigins()`). The grant providers (`impersonate`, `sso`, `remember`) refuse an account whose world is not the host's, a session presented on the other world's host is no session (`token.worldMismatch`, recomputed every request), and `/api/auth/remember/refresh` declines before rotating. E-mail links open the product the recipient's account lives in (`originForWorld` / `appUrlFor(orgId)`; byte-identical for INTERNSHIP), invitations are keyed by (address, organization), and reset, verification, erasure and e-mail change act on exactly the row they were minted for. The failed-sign-in counter stays shared by address on purpose, and moving an organization to the other product is refused (`409 vertical_move_email_conflict`) when its people already hold an account there. The marketing register page tells an invitee that an invitation for an address already used in the other product creates a separate account. `db push` drops the global unique on `User.email` and adds `(email, orgId)` — appliable, no data loss. The deliberate enumeration trade (`WRONG_WORLD_*` confirms an account to the holder of its password) is recorded in `docs/security-exceptions.md`; the whole model, the local-dev recipe and the known limits are in `docs/worlds.md`.

en: One e-mail address can now have an account in Internship CRM and another in SaleVali at the same time. The site you sign in on decides which one you get: interncrm.com opens Internship CRM, marketing.bcsit-gmbh.de opens SaleVali, and your session stays in that product.
Entering the right password on the wrong site no longer says "invalid email or password". It tells you which product your account is in and links straight to its sign-in page.
tr: Aynı e-posta adresiyle artık hem Internship CRM'de hem SaleVali'de ayrı birer hesabın olabilir. Hangisine gireceğini oturum açtığın site belirler: interncrm.com Internship CRM'i, marketing.bcsit-gmbh.de SaleVali'yi açar ve oturumun o üründe kalır.
Doğru parolayı yanlış sitede girmek artık "e-posta veya parola hatalı" demiyor. Hesabının hangi üründe olduğunu söylüyor ve doğrudan o ürünün giriş sayfasına bağlantı veriyor.
de: Dieselbe E-Mail-Adresse kann jetzt gleichzeitig ein Konto in Internship CRM und ein weiteres in SaleVali haben. Welches Konto geöffnet wird, entscheidet die Seite, auf der die Anmeldung erfolgt: interncrm.com öffnet Internship CRM, marketing.bcsit-gmbh.de öffnet SaleVali, und die Sitzung bleibt in diesem Produkt.

Wer das richtige Passwort auf der falschen Seite eingibt, sieht nicht mehr „E-Mail oder Passwort ungültig“. Stattdessen steht dort, in welchem Produkt das Konto liegt, mit einem Link direkt zu dessen Anmeldeseite.
